use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

evidence_cards.content: PPLI data available from J2 messages shall be used by C² JUs to reduce the redundancy of surveillance track reporting.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the high-level objective (goal) for the C² JU regarding PPLI data integration: reducing redundancy in surveillance track reporting.

evidence_cards.content: The protocols in this section are to be followed in order to minimize occurrences and duration of dual designations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement explicitly defines the high-level objective (goal) of the use case regarding common tracking and correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to process two tracks for dual designation resolution after they successfully pass the second correlation test and have no correlation restriction.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement explicitly defines the high-level goal of the use case: achieving dual designation resolution through track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The objective of track correlation is to prevent or eliminate dual designations by ensuring that each ballistic missile track reported on the interface represents a single data point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Directly defines the high-level goal of the use case 'Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation'.

evidence_cards.content: The goal of the use case is to resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly states the objective the C2 JU initiates action to achieve (resolving dual designations via track correlation).

evidence_cards.content: PPLI data available from J2 messages shall be used by C² JUs to reduce the redundancy of surveillance track reporting.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that PPLI data must be available and integrated into the system before correlation actions can occur — a necessary precondition for resolving dual designations via track correlation as described in the use case goal.

evidence_cards.content: A surveillance JU will accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and perform the applicable correlation and conflict processing necessary to ensure that duplicative information is not being transmitted on the Surveillance Network PG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms that the system (surveillance JU) must have already accepted PPLI data and performed initial correlation/conflict processing — a required state before any further correlation-based resolution of dual designations can proceed.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the mandatory system capability (automatic correlation) that must exist before the process of resolving dual designations via track correlation can begin.

evidence_cards.content: Correlation testing consists of position, velocity, and altitude tests.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system state (availability of these three test types) required before correlation can be performed.

evidence_cards.content: Positions of all tracks and IUs tested for correlation shall be extrapolated to the same time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a mandatory data synchronization precondition that must hold before the correlation test occurs.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall be eligible for correlation if they pass the following positional test: Course Differential (f), Speed Differential (g), and Altitude Differential (h).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the mandatory state where two tracks must satisfy specific positional criteria to be considered 'eligible' before the correlation use case can proceed.

evidence_cards.content: Tracks with TQ less than or equal to e are not eligible for correlation, except for new local real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exclusionary condition regarding track quality (TQ) that serves as a precondition for eligibility.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates that the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a mandatory system state restriction regarding ID conflicts that must be satisfied (or inhibited via parameter) before automatic correlation can proceed to resolve dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition involving Mode II codes that prevents automatic correlation, acting as a precondition for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if both are locally derived real-time tracks being updated with local positional data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a track source status (locally derived real-time) that restricts automatic correlation, serving as a precondition check.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1 (unless set to No Statement).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a data field constraint (Strength > 1) that inhibits automatic correlation, which must be evaluated before the use case proceeds.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall pass the correlation tests and restrictions in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and 4.4.4.3.1g 2(1-2,1) times before the correlation is executed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the state (passing specific tests a specific number of times) that must hold before the correlation process can be executed, satisfying the definition of a precondition for this use case.

evidence_cards.content: Track correlation prevents/eliminates dual designations by comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, boost indication) with data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the system capability and functional context required for the C2 JU to perform track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: Each C2 JU has the responsibility to determine whether data points detected by its local sensors are currently reported on the interface and if there are any conflicts between locally derived information and information reported on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific operational state and responsibility of the primary actor that must exist before resolving dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the system state (recognition of eligibility) required before the JU initiates action to resolve dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: A TN pair is determined to be a dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific condition (dual designation determination) that must exist for the use case to proceed.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall perform correlation tests in response to correlation requests from other units.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly identifies the trigger for the use case: a correlation request received from another unit initiates the C2 JU’s action of performing correlation tests, which is the start of resolving dual designations via track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation process is triggered by the 'next correlation stimulus', which initiates a second test of the two tracks that previously passed the initial tests.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event ('next correlation stimulus') that starts the use case execution after preconditions are met.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU determines whether data points detected by its local sensors are currently reported on the interface and if there are any conflicts between locally derived information and information reported on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific action/event that initiates the correlation process to resolve dual designations: the detection of a conflict or comparison between local and interface data.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the triggering event (recognition of eligible tracks) and the resulting actor action (initiating resolution) that starts the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific action sequence that initiates the main flow of the use case: comparing local vs. remote data to resolve dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies that the interaction is performed automatically by the system actor as part of the normal flow.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall pass the correlation tests and restrictions in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and 4.4.4.3.1g 2(1-2,1) times before the correlation is executed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific number of test passes required to initiate the main flow sequence.

evidence_cards.content: When two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they shall be deemed a tentative correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the intermediate state (tentative correlation) achieved during the first step of the multi-step process.

evidence_cards.content: The same two tracks shall be tested again upon the next correlation stimulus.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the action taken after the initial tentative correlation to proceed toward final resolution.

evidence_cards.content: If the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they shall be processed for dual designation resolution in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1j and k.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the success boundary where the system proceeds to resolve the dual designation.

evidence_cards.content: Each C2 JU must continuously correlate locally derived ballistic missile tracks with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the continuous action required of the actor to maintain track integrity and resolve dual designations as part of the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: In the event of conflict, the C2 JU shall resolve the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific resolution mechanism (main flow step) the actor performs when a correlation conflict is detected.

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks; the message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action taken by the actor to initiate resolution after recognizing eligible tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the standard system response (acceptance) that completes the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the final step in the sequence where the track is formally dropped from the system.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU participating on the Surveillance Network PG shall attempt to correlate received PPLI reports with data being received from local sensors.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the first step in the main flow: initiating correlation between incoming PPLI and local sensor tracks.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which the C2 JU has R², the J7.2 Correlation message shall be transmitted with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), and with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the system’s response when the C2 JU owns the correlated track — it retains its own track and drops the PPLI-sourced one, signaling non-acceptance of reverse correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This completes the resolution action by stopping redundant reporting of the dropped track, fulfilling the success boundary of resolving dual designation.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful path where ownership lies with another C2 JU but track numbers differ — still results in retaining PPLI source and dropping local surveillance track.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies behavior when track numbers match — typically accepts PPLI unless quality is zero, then reverts to accepting local surveillance track; represents conditional branching within main flow based on data quality.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the first step of the main flow for track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall make an automatic correlation test either upon receipt of each remote real-time J3.2 or J3.3 track (or J2.0/J2.2/J2.3 PPLI report) not confirmed to have existing correlation, or immediately prior to each transmission of a local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the trigger conditions and timing for the automatic correlation tests within the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they shall be deemed a tentative correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the first step in the main flow sequence for track correlation leading to dual designation resolution.

evidence_cards.content: The same two tracks shall be tested again upon the next correlation stimulus.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the mandatory second test step required before proceeding to dual designation resolution.

evidence_cards.content: If the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they shall be processed for dual designation resolution in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1j and k.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the final successful completion step of the main flow where dual designation resolution occurs after passing all tests.

evidence_cards.content: The process of correlation consists of comparing locally derived sensor data (e.g., position, velocity, boost indication) with the data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the core action sequence for resolving dual designations by correlating track data.

evidence_cards.content: In order to eliminate dual designations, it is imperative that each ballistic missile track reported on the interface represent a single data point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the success condition and boundary for the main flow interaction.

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall initiate transmission of the J7.2 message with the Retained TN/Dropped TN selection in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.1j.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the first step of the main flow: initiating the correlation message upon dual designation determination.

evidence_cards.content: If a selection conflict occurs due to OCCs on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception condition within the initiation step that prevents successful completion.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the system's response to the transmitted message, indicating acceptance is the default action barring specific restrictions.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies...
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the specific handling for manually initiated correlations (RV=3) as part of the flow.

evidence_cards.content: A manual capability shall be provided to initiate the correlation of any two tracks irrespective of the correlation test criteria in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f, the correlation restrictions in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g, or the requirements in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1h.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a successful alternative path (Manual Correlation) that diverges from the main flow by bypassing standard automated eligibility tests and restrictions.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the boundary conditions under which the manual correlation alternative flow is prohibited, ensuring the variant remains within valid operational constraints.

evidence_cards.content: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) Change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation, or (b) Transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a successful alternative path where the main flow's automatic correlation is blocked by an ID conflict, but can proceed via manual intervention (changing data or transmitting a report).

evidence_cards.content: JUs may apply one exception to the restriction in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1g(1) and 4.4.4.3.1g(7)(a) above. If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, and that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific variant/exception to the standard 'ID Conflict' restriction found in the preconditions, allowing automatic correlation to proceed (resolving dual designation) despite the presence of conflicting IDs under specific engagement conditions.

evidence_cards.content: When a J7.2 message is initiated by own unit and a Drop Track message has not yet been received for the Dropped TN, it shall be retained as a remote track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative flow path where the originating unit retains the dropped track locally as a remote track pending confirmation, diverging from the standard immediate drop.

evidence_cards.content: If the Identity (ID) or Identity Amplifying Descriptor (IAD) of retained TN and Dropped TN are different and the difference would result in automatic acceptance of the Dropped TN ID/IAD, the Dropped TN ID/IAD and Special Interest Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type shall be transferred to Retained TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific data transfer variant within the correlation process based on identity conflict rules being 'Not Inhibited'.

evidence_cards.content: When the Identity of Retained TN and Dropped TN are the same, associated identification data reported for the Retained TN shall be retained.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative data retention behavior when identities match, ensuring existing data is preserved rather than overwritten.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative flow where the originating unit performs a specific track drop action (J7.0) as part of the correlation resolution process, diverging from the standard acceptance flow.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2, Correlation Rejection, shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative recovery path following a rejection event, specifying a time-based constraint on retrying the correlation request.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative human-in-the-loop intervention step triggered by a rejection during manual correlation attempts.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This details an alternative successful path where the receiving unit proposes a different track retention strategy (reverse correlation) instead of simply accepting or rejecting.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, and the Dropped TN has an OCC, if RV is set to 3, the system shall execute the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative processing logic for handling correlation requests when track ownership differs from the message parameters, specifically for manually initiated correlations (RV=3).

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow where correlation is attempted but results in a reverse correlation response (RV=1) due to ownership conflict, diverging from standard acceptance path.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception condition based on Geodetic Position Quality value that reverses normal data acceptance behavior — discarding PPLI instead of J3 data.

evidence_cards.content: Subsurface tracks shall not be correlated with IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Explicitly excludes subsurface tracks from correlation process entirely, representing a terminal exception condition preventing any correlation attempt.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines explicit exception conditions under which manual correlation (an alternative flow action) is prohibited, constituting an exception path that prevents successful dual designation resolution via manual means.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This imposes a temporal constraint on correlation testing; failure to meet this timing requirement would constitute an exception condition preventing valid correlation execution.

evidence_cards.content: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) Change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation, or (b) Transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception handling path when a specific correlation restriction (conflicting IDs) prevents automatic resolution, requiring operator intervention.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU receiving a J7.2 Correlation message and also holding OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks (if the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled) shall reject the correlation in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.2a(1).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system response (rejection) when a receiving unit encounters a correlation request that violates its own Operational Contingency Constraints or ID conflict restrictions.

evidence_cards.content: Track decorrelation should occur when it is determined more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific condition (existence of multiple data points) that triggers an exception to the single-track goal, requiring decorrelation instead of correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The situations most likely to lead to dual ballistic missile designations are: Initial report on ballistic missile contacts, Track merging, Simultaneous multiple launches, Existence of registration errors, Time of observation differences, and High velocity contacts.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Enumerates specific error conditions or unexpected scenarios (e.g., registration errors, time differences) that constitute exceptions leading to dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected (RV field set to value 2), the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific recovery action required when the main flow fails due to rejection.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN and the correlation is abandoned due to OCC conflict on both tracks, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the cleanup procedure when the correlation process is terminated early due to conflicting ownership constraints.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines explicit exception conditions that prevent manual correlation initiation — these are terminal blocking constraints for the alternative flow path where manual override would otherwise bypass normal test criteria.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a hard temporal boundary for correlation testing; exceeding this window constitutes an exception condition that may invalidate the correlation attempt or require re-extrapolation.

evidence_cards.content: JUs may apply one exception to the restriction in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1g(1) and 4.4.4.3.1g(7)(a): if either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition under which a normally prohibited correlation (due to ID conflict or engagement status constraint) is permitted — this constitutes an exception flow that overrides standard restrictions.

evidence_cards.content: The Unknown/Hostile track shall be the dropped Track Number (TN-2). This exception allows breaking the engagement and/or destroying missile(s) in flight.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the outcome of the exception: which track is dropped and the operational rationale (breaking engagement/destroying missiles), confirming this is a controlled deviation from normal correlation rules.

evidence_cards.content: This exception shall not be applied by any JU upon receipt of a J7.2 Correlation message. Thus, any JU receiving a J7.2 Correlation message and also holding OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks (if the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled) shall reject the correlation in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.2a(1).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a terminal rejection condition for the exception flow — if a J7.2 message is received while constraints exist, correlation must be rejected, establishing a hard boundary for when the exception cannot proceed.

evidence_cards.content: Track decorrelation should occur when it is determined more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception handling path (decorrelation) triggered by the condition of multiple data points existing for a single track, which is the inverse of the successful correlation flow.

evidence_cards.content: A ballistic missile track is considered lost when the JU with R² does not receive any local sensor data since the last transmitted update, or the JU determines that the track is lost by other system criteria.

evidence_cards.content: Ballistic missile track data will not be extrapolated except as specified in accordance with paragraph 4.4.6.13.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a constraint on data availability during track loss — no extrapolation unless explicitly permitted — which may prevent successful correlation if real-time or interpolated data is required for the second correlation test.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies that rejection is a valid exception path when specific prespecified conditions are met, diverging from the main flow acceptance step.

evidence_cards.content: Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system response (RV=2) and action required when an exception (rejection) occurs.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field is set to value 1, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a condition where a reverse correlation attempt results in rejection, constituting an exception flow outcome.

evidence_cards.content: Correlation shall be rejected if the Retained TN and Dropped TN decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once.

evidence_cards.content: Correlation shall be rejected if both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC (Operational Control Constraint).

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Indicates that loss of track — a potential exception condition during correlation or tracking — is explicitly addressed as a reporting requirement, relevant to exception flow handling.

evidence_cards.content: Track decorrelation should occur when it is determined more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception condition (detection of multiple data points for a single reported track) and the required system response (decorrelation), which constitutes an error-handling path to correct or prevent dual designations after correlation has been attempted or assumed.

evidence_cards.content: Situations most likely to lead to dual ballistic missile designations — including initial reports, track merging, simultaneous multiple launches, registration errors, time of observation differences, and high velocity contacts — represent conditions under which correlation may fail or produce erroneous results, triggering exception handling.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies specific operational scenarios that serve as triggers for exception flows where standard correlation logic may not suffice or may produce invalid outcomes, requiring special handling or rejection paths.

evidence_cards.content: A JU reporting a ballistic missile track with the Lost Track Indicator field set to value 1 (Lost Track) is assumed to have a TQ of 5 less than that being reported; for example, if a JU is reporting 'Lost Track' data with a TQ of 15, a JU holding 'Tracking' data may assume R² with a TQ of 11.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception handling rule for resolving dual designations when one track is lost, allowing a tracking unit to assume reporting responsibility based on calculated reliability values rather than standard time tags.

evidence_cards.content: A JU assumes R² if it has not received a remote report on a locally held track for 25 seconds, provided the last remote report was received with the Lost Track Indicator set to value 0 (Tracking).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a timeout-based exception flow where reporting responsibility automatically reverts to the local holder after a communication lapse during active tracking.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R² for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific exception path where the system handles track ownership differently than the standard correlation acceptance flow by dropping the track locally and signaling cessation of reporting.

evidence_cards.content: Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the explicit error handling mechanism and message format used when the primary success scenario fails due to rejection conditions.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2, Correlation Rejection, shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the recovery behavior and time-based constraint imposed on the system following an exception event (correlation rejection).

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This identifies a specific exception handler action (alerting the operator) triggered by a failed manual correlation attempt.

evidence_cards.content: If the received J7.2 message contains one or both of the same TNs as contained in the transmission of the own unit J7.2 message sequence in progress, the following actions shall be taken.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This introduces a conflict resolution exception flow for handling simultaneous or overlapping correlation requests involving the same tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The dual designation is resolved via correlation; the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the successful end state of the use case: the two tracks have been correlated into one, resolving the dual designation. The dropped track (TN-2) is no longer maintained as an independent entity for that unit, fulfilling the success boundary defined in the goal.

evidence_cards.content: If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, and that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed despite the restriction, with the Unknown/Hostile track being the dropped Track Number (TN-2).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a variant postcondition where correlation succeeds under an exception rule, resulting in a specific track (Unknown/Hostile) being designated as the dropped one, thereby altering the standard outcome based on ID conflict restrictions.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful correlation execution, the Dropped TN is designated as a common local track if the own unit holds it as a local or common local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the final disposition of the dropped track number for the owning unit in a specific ownership scenario.

evidence_cards.content: If the own unit has R2 for the Dropped TN, it transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message; if the Dropped TN is subsequently reported by another IU, the own unit retains it as a remote track and does not reattempt correlation for 60 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the final state and behavior regarding the dropped track when the own unit held responsibility (R2).

evidence_cards.content: Specific data fields from the Dropped TN are transferred to the Retained TN upon correlation execution: Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, Altitude Source, TQ, and Strength (if the Dropped TN was a local or common local track).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the resulting data state of the retained track immediately following successful correlation.

evidence_cards.content: Identification data transfer depends on ID conflict restrictions: if restricted and IDs differ, the last Identity reported for the Dropped TN is processed as an Identity Difference Report for the Retained TN; otherwise, specific ID/IAD and platform attributes are transferred.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the rules governing the final identification data state of the retained track.

evidence_cards.content: Any nonzero Mode I, II, or III IFF/SIF data from the Dropped TN is transferred to the Retained TN if the corresponding data for the Retained TN is zero.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the condition under which IFF/SIF data is merged into the retained track's final state.

evidence_cards.content: The reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the successful end state of the correlation process: eliminating dual designations results in a single data point representation for the track.

evidence_cards.content: In order to eliminate dual designations, it is imperative that each ballistic missile track reported on the interface represent a single data point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Reinforces the postcondition that the system must achieve a state where tracks are represented as single data points to satisfy the goal of resolving dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: Upon acceptance of the requested correlation, the receiving IUs retain the designated Retained TN and drop the designated Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary state change of the tracks involved in the dual designation resolution.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it drops the Dropped TN and transmits the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a concrete action and state change (dropping the track) required of the originating unit upon successful correlation.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV field set to value 3), the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
